bullets.title: PLTR: Blowout 2Q with US Commercial +149% YoY; FY guide raised to $8.15B—consensus $220-245 PT range
bullets.body: Palantir posted Q2 revenue of $1.94B (+93% YoY), beating $1.81B consensus; adj. EPS $0.41 beat $0.35 est. US Commercial accelerated to +149% YoY (from +133%) and Government +90% YoY; TCV bookings +153% YoY. FY26 revenue guide raised to $8.15-8.16B from $7.65-7.66B (+82% YoY), US Commercial guide to >134%. FCF margin 63%; non-GAAP operating margin ~62%. Street PT actions: UBS $220 (46x '28E FCF), Citi $245 (67x '28E FCF), Piper OW $230, Mizuho $215, Morgan Stanley $205. CEO internal target for US Commercial to approach >100% growth over next 18 months. Q3 '26 expense elevated from seasonal hiring and marketing.

bullets.title: Chinese optical transceiver import ban lifts COHR +18%, LITE +14%, FN +14%, GLW +10%, MRVL +8%
bullets.body: Trump administration drafting ban on U.S. imports of new Chinese data center optical transceiver models (FCC involved). Chinese supplier Innolight holds ~27% global share; ban would force U.S. hyperscalers to domestic suppliers like Coherent and Lumentum, near-term supply constraints expected. ANET also moved higher on data center read-through. JPM notes Innolight market share and higher costs for buyers as key near-term concerns.

bullets.title: SPOT 2Q: Gross margin beats (33.4% vs 33.1%), but Q3 MAU guide 788M misses 794M consensus—shares down
bullets.body: Spotify 2Q operating income €655M beat €638M est on 30bps gross margin beat and lower social charges. MAUs 777M were 1M below guide; Premium Subs 300M beat. Q3 guide: revenue €5.0B above est, but MAUs 788M well below 794-795M consensus implying only 11M net adds vs 16M in 2Q. 3Q OI €670M slightly below consensus. AI licensing deal with Merlin announced as paid add-on tier. Multiple analysts (JPM OW, UBS Buy, Citi Buy $620, Wolfe OW $690) constructive but flag MAU deceleration. Shares indicated -4% pre-market.

bullets.title: W (Wayfair) 2Q beat: revenue +8.7% YoY, EBITDA $242M above est; active customers resume growth; Buy maintained
bullets.body: Wayfair Q2 revenue $3.52B beat $3.47B est (+7.5%); adj. EPS $0.95 beat $0.90; adj. EBITDA $242M beat $230M est. US revenue +8.7%, active customers +3.3% YoY (second consecutive quarter of growth after six-quarter decline), orders +6% YoY. Specialty brands grew ~20%, Perigold >35%. Margin beat of 16bps but incremental adj. EBITDA margins ~15% vs 22% in 1Q due to ad reinvestment—flagged as underwhelming. UBS Buy PT $118 (~18x '27E EBITDA). Q3 revenue expected in mid-single-digit range. International -1.3% softer.

bullets.title: TKO 2Q: AEBITDA $650M beats; raises FY AEBITDA guide to $2.275-2.305B; UFC partnerships key driver
bullets.body: TKO Q2 revenue $1.55B (+18% YoY) and adj. EBITDA $650M (+23%) both beat. FY26 guidance raised $75M on revenue and $25M on EBITDA. UFC revenue +29% YoY driven by White House partnerships ($145M); WWE +12% YoY on media rights growth. IMG benefiting from World Cup. Company completed $1B buyback and announced additional $1B+ authorization. UBS Buy PT $238 (20x '27E EBITDA); JPM OW $222. Management focused on execution, no M&A.

bullets.title: AMD Q3 data center segment modeled at $8.08B (+21% QoQ) as ANET buyside expects FY26 guide raise to $11.7-12.2B
bullets.body: AMD data center segment Q3 modeled at $8.08B by UBS's Tim Arcuri; Arcuri's C2028E EPS of $27.57 vs Street $19. Buyside positioning still high post-AI day with shorts ticking up; buyside expects $30 C28 EPS vs conservative consensus. ANET sentiment turned cautious on growth/competition and component shortages; stock +33% off lows at 41x forward earnings. ANET bulls cite strong XPO feedback, growing backlog, FY27 EPS growth potentially >40%; 70% of buyside expect FY26 revenue guide raised to $11.7-12.2B vs current $11.5B. ANET deferred revenue exiting Mar-26 at $3.6B.

bullets.title: SNAP 2Q beat: revenue +19% YoY, EBITDA $250M (30% above guidance); NA DAUs stabilize; Specs launch Sept 16
bullets.body: Snap Q2 revenue $1.60B beat $1.54B est; adj. EBITDA $250M beat $192M guidance high end. NA DAUs 92M flat Q/Q after three quarters of declines; ad revenue +9% YoY with large advertiser rebound. Subscription + Other revenues +85% YoY ($316M, ~20% of total). Q3 guidance: revenue $1.70-1.74B in-line, EBITDA $300-350M at midpoint slightly soft. JPM maintains Underweight $6 PT on durability concerns; Citi Neutral/HR; MS EW $7 PT; Mizuho raises to $6. Specs commercial launch September 16.

bullets.title: FOXA-ROKU deal analysis: JPM Neutral on execution risks; $70 PT implies 10.9x FY28E EBITDA
bullets.body: Fox is acquiring Roku at $160/share with 40% FOXA equity consideration. Deal improves Fox's growth profile to 7% EBITDA CAGR (FY26-29E) vs prior flat/negative trajectory. Pro forma entity becomes third-largest streaming platform behind YouTube (13%) and Disney (11%). Deal is 10% FCF dilutive in Year 1, near breakeven Year 2, +8% accretive Year 3. Pro forma leverage rises to 2.9x at close. JPM Neutral pending NFL renewal visibility and synergy clarity. FOXA shares fell ~30% since announcement.

bullets.title: AAPL: Two downgrades on same day—China Renaissance to Hold ($280 PT from $329), DZ Bank to Hold
bullets.body: China Renaissance Securities downgraded Apple to Hold from Buy, cutting PT to $280 from $329 (8% downside vs $303 current), citing FactSet consensus $327 average target. DZ Bank separately downgraded AAPL to Hold, maintaining $310 PT (2% upside). MacBook Air reportedly facing shortage from memory chip supply constraints per Nikkei. India sales topped $10B annually for first time.

bullets.title: CRWV: Piper initiates Overweight at $151 PT on AI infrastructure early-mover advantage and NVIDIA relationship
bullets.body: Piper Sandler's Jim Fish initiates CoreWeave (CRWV) at Overweight with $151 PT, favoring it over co-initiated NBIS Neutral ($224 PT) due to NBIS's Vineland datacenter risk. CRWV and NBIS positioned to benefit from AI infrastructure buildout demand>supply with NVIDIA relationships and architectures delivering >40% lower costs vs hyperscalers.

bullets.title: NVDA: DRAM shortage to persist through 2027; Rubin Ultra HBM despec confirmed as supply issue not demand; Huawei warns on physical limits
bullets.body: TrendForce reports DRAM/HBM capacity at SK Hynix, Micron, and Samsung sold out through 2027 with customers allocated 60-70% of requested volumes; NAND bookings to fill by year-end. NVDA reportedly considering downgrading Rubin Ultra HBM from 12Hi to 8Hi configuration—confirmed as supply-driven capacity optimization, not demand issue. Separately, Huawei top scientist warns NVDA approaching physical semiconductor scaling limits. Anthropic signed $10B computing deal with Volta Infra Holdings.

bullets.title: WIX 2Q: Revenue beats by ~1.5%, FCF 58% above est; Base44 GM guided to ~60% in 2H26; UW maintained by JPM
bullets.body: Wix Q2 revenue $563M beat consensus by ~1.5%; FCF ex-acquisitions $61.2M ~58% above estimates. Base44 AI costs depressed Creative Subscription GM -470bps YoY to 80.4% in 2Q. FY26 bookings guidance maintained at low-teens YoY. Base44 non-GAAP GM expected at ~60% in 2H26. JPM UW $62 PT cites ongoing Partners revenue deceleration; UBS Neutral; Citi Neutral $59 PT on 6x '27E EV/EBITDA.

bullets.title: ALAB: Citi constructive ahead of 4-Aug earnings; 3% revenue upside and 9% EPS upside expected on retimer demand
bullets.body: Citi semiconductor analyst Papa Sylla is constructive on Astera Labs (ALAB) ahead of Q2 earnings, expecting 3% revenue upside and 9% EPS upside vs consensus. Upside driven by continued retimer demand with higher AI accelerator expectations and Taurus/Scorpio product ramps. 1M implied vol at 93rd percentile but 5.2 points below realized. UBS raises Trn3 unit estimates to 1.8MM/2.8MM units for C26/C27 but notes caution on C28/29 as AWS migrates from NeuronLink toward NVLink/UALink.

bullets.title: AMZN: Bezos files to sell $4.07B (~15M shares) under Rule 10b5-1 plan; AWS capacity sold through 2028
bullets.body: Jeff Bezos filed Form 144 to sell up to 15M Amazon shares (~$4.07B) under a pre-arranged 10b5-1 trading plan. Separately, Amazon AWS chief Matt Garman stated on Bloomberg that demand for AI-linked services is 'just massive' with capacity already spoken for through 2027 and into 2028. Amazon received $600M in tariff refunds per Bloomberg. Amazon custom silicon hitting $25B annual run rate. AMZN market cap briefly crossed $3T for the first time.

bullets.title: T/VZ/CMCSA capex: Telco +13% YoY in 2Q; fiber scaling aggressively; VZ signed $1B+ Google dark-fiber deal
bullets.body: JPM tracks US telco/cable capex with aggregate service provider capex +13% YoY in Q2 ($12.8B), above est. FY26 guides reiterated: AT&T $23-24B, T-Mobile ~$10B, Verizon $16-16.5B. VZ announced $1B+ Google dark-fiber deal with multi-billion multi-year follow-ons expected. CMCSA noted broadband downstream traffic +10% YoY, upstream +25% YoY partly from AI queries. Cable aggregate capex +8% YoY to ~$5.2B. Charter targeting <$8B capex in 2028 vs ~$11.5B today.

bullets.title: MSFT: trading above 200-day MA at widest margin since October; hyperscaler cloud capex tracker points to +29% YoY growth in 2027
bullets.body: MSFT trading above its 200-day moving average at the widest margin since October per chart analysis. Morgan Stanley's hyperscaler cloud capex tracker revised to 29% YoY growth in 2027 vs prior 14% after all four US hyperscalers (META, AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT) express greater confidence in CY26-27 ROIC supported by rising backlogs and pricing power. JPM bullish on hyperscalers: Andy Jassy signals AWS could become $1T+ revenue business.

bullets.title: SNDK: Partners with SK Hynix on industry-first HBF standard specs; GOOGL joins consortium
bullets.body: SK Hynix and SanDisk unveiled the industry's first standard specifications for high-bandwidth flash (HBF) six months after launching the consortium. Google and Tenstorrent have joined the consortium. HBF is positioned as a memory layer between HBM and SSDs enabling HBM-speed data transfer with greater capacity for AI inference and large model weights. SNDK also partnering on High Bandwidth Flash standardization.

bullets.title: INTU downgraded at Truist; NOW -2.8%; HUBS and SHOP: earnings setups favor buying weakness
bullets.body: Truist downgraded Intuit (INTU) adding to pre-market pressure. Cloudflare (NET) PT raised to $290 from $225 at Jefferies; stock up 44% since 1Q earnings and investors want 34%+ YoY acceleration in 2Q. SHOP investors want 30%+ GP$ growth in Q2 and mid-to-high 20s guidance for Q3; HUBS sentiment more positive with investors wanting full Q2 beat passed through to 2026 guidance. Wolfe SaaS index at 5.3x FY+2 EV/Sales with +5.6% week-over-week multiple expansion; IGV -10.5% YTD vs S&P 500 +10.1%.

bullets.title: MU: 2027 DRAM/HBM production capacity fully sold out; lawsuit challenges NY permit for Micron facility
bullets.body: DigiTimes and multiple sources confirm SK Hynix, Micron, and Samsung 2027 DRAM and HBM annual capacity is fully booked with customers receiving only 60-70% of requested volumes. NAND flash bookings expected complete by year-end. Counterpoint Q2 DRAM data shows SK Hynix revenue-based market share only ~1 percentage point ahead of Micron driven by HBM3E pricing dynamics. Separately, a lawsuit filed challenging New York's permit approval process for Micron's planned chip facility.

bullets.title: ORCL: Oracle's credit default swap spread hits historic high, exceeding 2008 GFC peak; Oracle providing 22.6% of China's known AI compute
bullets.body: Oracle's CDS spread rose to its highest level in company history, surpassing levels seen during the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, per social media data. Separately, Oracle was reportedly providing 22.6% of China's known AI computing power per Bloomberg reporting.
